source_text: Orantes autem non infructuosis nec nudis precibus ad Deum . ueniant. inefficax petitio est, cum precatur Deum sterilis oratio. nam cum omnis arbor non faciens fructum excidatur et in ignem mittatur, utique et sermo non habens fructum promereri Deum non potest, quia nulla operatione fecundus est. et ideo scriptura diuina instruit dicens: bona est oratio cum ieiunio et eleemosyna. nam qui in die iudicii praemium pro operibus et eleemosynis redditurus est hodie quoque ad orationem cum operatione uenienti benignus auditor est. sic denique Cornelius centurio cum oraret, meruit audiri. fuit faciens multas eleemosynas in plebem et semper orans Deum. huic circa horam nonam oranti adstitit angelus testimonium reddens sui operis et dicens: Corneli, orationes tuae et eleemosynae tuae ascenderunt ad memoriam coram Deo.
thought_title: Prayer must be fruitful and joined with good works
orientation: Cyprian is urging that prayer must not be empty but accompanied by good works, and he introduces Cornelius as an example of prayer joined with almsgiving.
pass_a_gloss: Praying [ones] however not [with] unfruitful nor bare prayers to God let [them] come. Ineffective [a] petition is, when [one] prays to God [a] barren prayer. For when every tree not making fruit is cut down and into fire is thrown, certainly also [a] word not having fruit to merit God not is able, because [by] no working fruitful it is. And therefore [the] scripture divine instructs saying: good is prayer with fasting and almsgiving. For [he] who on [the] day of judgment [a] reward for works and almsgivings [is] about to give back today also to prayer with working [to one] coming [a] kind hearer is. Thus finally [the] centurion Cornelius when he prayed, deserved to be heard. He was [one] doing many almsgivings among [the] people and always praying [to] God. To this [one] around [the] ninth hour [while] praying stood by [an] angel testimony giving back of his work and saying: Cornelius, prayers your and almsgivings your have ascended to remembrance before God.

choices.why: Keeps the two adjectives distinct: 'infructuosis' as unfruitful and 'nudis' as bare, preserving the image of prayer lacking the clothing of good works.
Renders 'sterilis' as barren to preserve the agricultural metaphor of fruitlessness, matching the tree image that follows.
Keeps the verb 'promereri' as 'merit' with God as direct object, preserving Cyprian's strong claim that fruitless speech cannot win God's favor.
Renders 'benignus auditor' literally as 'kind hearer' to preserve the image of God listening favorably to prayer joined with work.
Keeps the Roman time reference literally as 'ninth hour' rather than converting to modern time, preserving the biblical setting.

choices.english: giving testimony of his own work
choices.why: Renders 'sui operis' as 'his own work' to preserve the reflexive possessive, showing the angel testifying to Cornelius's own deeds.

pass_b_english: Those who pray should not come to God with unfruitful and bare prayers. A petition is ineffective when a barren prayer is offered to God. For since every tree that does not produce fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire, so too a word that has no fruit cannot merit God, because it is fruitful through no work. And therefore the divine Scripture instructs, saying: “Prayer is good with fasting and almsgiving” (Tobit 12:8). For he who on the day of judgment will give reward for works and almsgiving is today also a kind hearer to the one who comes to prayer with work. Thus finally the centurion Cornelius, when he prayed, deserved to be heard. He was one who did many almsgivings among the people and always prayed to God. To him, praying about the ninth hour, an angel stood by, giving testimony of his work and saying: “Cornelius, your prayers and your almsgivings have ascended as a memorial before God” (Acts 10:3-4).

problems.quote: because it is made fruitful by no work
problems.why: Latin says 'fecundus est' (is fruitful/fecund), not 'made fruitful'; it means the word lacks fruit because it has no work, not that work makes it fruitful.
problems.fix: because it is fruitful through no work
problems.ruling: Latin 'fecundus est' = 'is fruitful,' not 'made fruitful'; passive 'made' mistranslates the stative construction.

edits.old: because it is made fruitful by no work
edits.new: because it is fruitful through no work

fixed: Changed 'because it is made fruitful by no work' to 'because it is fruitful through no work' to match the Latin 'quia nulla operatione fecundus est', which states the word is fruitful through no work, not that it is made fruitful by work.

problems.quote: giving testimony of his own work
problems.why: sui operis refers to Cornelius's work, not the angel's own work; agency confused.

edits.old: giving testimony of his own work

fixed: Changed 'giving testimony of his own work' to 'giving testimony of his work': source 'testimonium reddens sui operis' refers to Cornelius's work, not the angel's own work.

last_rejected.quote: because it is fruitful through no work
last_rejected.why: Sense inverted: Latin says 'fruitful by no work' (i.e., barren), English says 'fruitful through no work' (double negative = fruitful).
last_rejected.fix: because it is barren, with no work to make it fruitful
last_rejected.ruling: 'fruitful through no work' means 'not fruitful by any work'—not a double negative; English correctly renders 'nulla operatione fecundus est'.

last_rejected.source_quote: bona est oratio cum ieiunio et eleemosyna
last_rejected.why: The quotation matches Tobit 12:8, but the source gives no citation; adding it is an editorial addition not in the Latin.
last_rejected.ruling: Adding scripture references is standard editorial practice in translations; not a translation error, and Tobit 12:8 is correct.
